paper.title: Optimal Analysis for Bandit Learning in Matching Markets with Serial Dictatorship

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit learning in (decentralized) two-sided matching markets under serial dictatorship
unmapped: Two-sided matching market: N players (learners) and K >= N arms; arms have known fixed preferences over players
Serial dictatorship: all arms share the same preference ranking over players (guarantees unique stable matching)
Collisions resolved by arms' preferences: only the most preferred proposing player is matched, others get reward 0
Players observe the full matching result each round
Decentralized: each player acts independently, knows N, K
Regret measured per player against its unique stable matched arm (stable regret)
All players' preferences are distinct (mu_{i,k} != mu_{i,k'})
Delta is the minimum gap over all players and all pairs of arms
settings.definition_quote: If player $p_i$ is successfully matched, it will receive a random reward $X_i(t)$, which is 1-subgaussian with mean $\mu_{i,\bar{A}_i(t)}$. If player $p_i$ is rejected, it will receive $X_i(t) = 0$. ... We consider the market satisfies serial dictatorship, where each arm shares the same preference. ... R_i(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T \mu_{i,m^\ast(i)} - \EE{\sum_{t=1}^{T}X_i(T)}

algorithms.name: Decentralized Multi-Level Successive Selection with elimination subroutine (MLSE)

symbols.i_rank: rank i of player p_i in the arms' common preference order
symbols.ell_i: rank of p_i's stable matched arm in p_i's own preference list (ell_i <= N)
symbols.Delta_mm: minimum reward gap across all players and all pairs of arms, min_{i,k,k'} |mu_{i,k}-mu_{i,k'}|

conditions: serial dictatorship (all arms share the same preference over players)

source.label: theorem: 1
source.quote: Following the multi-level successive selection algorithm (Algorithm \ref{alg:main}) with elimination subroutine, the stable regret of player $p_i \in \mathcal{N}$ satisfies R_{i}(T) \leq \frac{32i \log(T)}{\Delta^2} + \sum_{k=\ell_i+1}^{K}  \frac{32\log(T)}{\Delta_{i,\sigma_i(\ell_i),\sigma_i(k)}}  + 2NK + N +  \frac{32 i (N \log K + K)}{\Delta^2} \leq   \frac{32i \log(T)}{\Delta^2}+\frac{32(K-\ell_i) \log(T)}{\Delta}+2NK + N +  \frac{32 i (N \log K + K)}{\Delta^2}

results.notes: Per-player stable regret against unique stable matched arm (mapped to best_fixed_action). Regret defined via means minus expected rewards, i.e. pseudo-regret. The first (finer) form in the theorem replaces 32(K-ell_i)log T/Delta by sum_{k>ell_i} 32 log T/Delta_{i,sigma_i(ell_i),sigma_i(k)}. Since i <= N this gives O(N log T/Delta^2 + K log T/Delta). Appendix states ML-UCB attains the same O bound informally (not a formal statement).

symbols.i_rank: rank i of player p_i in the arms' common preference order
symbols.Delta_mm: minimum reward gap across all players and all pairs of arms

conditions: for every player i, its stable matched arm is its i-th favourite arm

source.quote: If for any player $i\in [N]$, its stable matched arm is its $i$-th favorite arm, then the regret for player $i$ is bounded by R_i(T) \leq N + \frac{32 (K-i) \log T}{\Delta} + 2NK + \frac{32 i (N \log K + K)}{\Delta^2}.

results.notes: Algorithm assumed to be MLSE (corollary follows Theorem 1).
